name: ABAP
title: ABAP (7.58)
lifecycleNote: SAP ships this language level inside current ABAP Platform releases

type.text: **Static typing is checked at activation**: A program is checked against the ABAP Dictionary types before it runs
**ABAP Objects gives interfaces and classes**: An interface names the methods, and a class implements them without multiple inheritance
**The Dictionary is the shared type system**: A data element, a domain, or a table type is defined once and referenced by every program
**A reference can be unbound**: A reference variable starts initial, and the type does not say so; a read without `IS BOUND` ends the program
**There are no sum types**: An alternative is a `CASE` over a type field or a set of flags, and the compiler does not check that every case is handled
**User code has no generics**: A routine that works for many types is written with field symbols or `TYPE ANY`, which the compiler cannot check
**Run-time type services expose the structure**: RTTI reads a type's components at run time, and `ASSIGN COMPONENT` reaches a field by name
**Two generations share one grammar**: A program can mix procedural statements with class-based code in the same include
**A call's effects are not in its type**: A signature says what a method returns, not what it writes to the database or the screen

construction.text: **A constructor is declared and checked**: `METHODS constructor` runs at `CREATE OBJECT`, and the class states its own invariants
**`CREATE OBJECT` separates construction from allocation**: The runtime allocates, and the class decides what the object holds
**A class attribute is shared state**: A `CLASS-DATA` attribute is reachable from every caller in the session
**Everything is mutable unless declared constant**: `DATA` is the default and `CONSTANTS` is opt-in, so an object's fields can change under a holder

memory.text: **The runtime manages memory**: Objects and internal tables are released by the ABAP runtime, and a program never frees storage by hand
**An internal table is the collection type**: A table is a typed container the runtime manages, and an index read is bounds-checked
**No destructor runs at scope exit**: A lock, a file, or a cursor is released by the logical unit of work or by an explicit close
**A large internal table lives in the session's memory**: The runtime's memory is bounded per work process, and a big table is a sizing decision

error.text: **Class-based exceptions are declared but not enforced**: A method can raise `CX_*`, and a caller is not required to handle it; a run-time error ends the program
**There is no result type**: A failure travels as an exception or as `sy-subrc`, and neither composes
**`sy-subrc` can be ignored**: The classic return code is set by a statement, and nothing forces the next statement to read it
**`TRY ... CATCH ... CLEANUP` gives a structured path**: A class-based exception is caught by type, and `CLEANUP` runs on the way out

concurrency.text: **A function module can start a new task**: `CALL FUNCTION ... STARTING NEW TASK` runs a unit in parallel, and `RECEIVE RESULTS` collects it
**Shared state is the default across sessions**: A database row, a shared memory area, or a lock object is reachable from every session, and nothing in the type marks it
**A lock object states the protocol**: An `ENQUEUE`/`DEQUEUE` pair names the object it protects, so the lock is a repository object
**The unit of work is the transaction**: A logical unit of work commits or rolls back as a whole, and a long dialog step holds it open

platform.text: **A program runs only inside an SAP system**: The ABAP runtime, the Dictionary, and the database interface are the platform, and there is no other host
**The database is abstracted**: Open SQL is translated by the database interface, so one program runs on HANA, Db2, Oracle, or SQL Server
**The kernel is the virtual machine**: The runtime executes the generated code and controls screens, events, and the database interface
**The cloud flavour restricts the language**: ABAP for Cloud Development permits a subset, so an on-premise program may not be allowed in the cloud

performance.text: **A program is interpreted from generated code**: The kernel executes the generated form, and there is no ahead-of-time path to machine code
**Code pushdown moves work to the database**: CDS views and Open SQL carry the set operation to the database instead of looping in ABAP
**A nested loop over two internal tables is the classic cost**: The code-pushdown guidance exists to replace that pattern
**Buffering holds hot data in the application server**: A table buffer keeps frequently read data in the server's memory

ecosystem.text: **The ecosystem belongs to one vendor**: SAP ships the language, the runtime, the tooling, and the applications, and no third party can implement ABAP
**One runtime and one framework dominate**: The SAP programming model, the Dictionary, and the transport system are the only route
**Decades of code remain in the repository**: A release keeps old syntax, old APIs, and old idioms working, so every new feature coexists with them
**ABAP Development Tools is a capable IDE**: Eclipse-based editing, syntax check, debugging, and transport are integrated
**abapGit brings version control**: A repository can be exported to Git, so a team can review changes outside the transport system

evolution.text: **The compatibility promise is strong**: A release keeps old statements working, so an upgrade rarely breaks a program
**New syntax is additive**: Inline declarations, constructor expressions, and CDS arrived without invalidating older code
**The repository accumulates every generation**: A system carries classic reports, function modules, and classes side by side
**The language level moves with the platform**: A program's language level changes when the system is upgraded, not on the program's schedule

domain.text: **The domain is enterprise business software**: A program models orders, invoices, and materials inside an ERP system
**Ordinary application work is expensive**: There is no general file, socket, or thread API in the language, so a task outside the business model is built from the runtime's interfaces
**The framework sets the architecture**: The dynpro or RESTful Application Programming model, the logical unit of work, and the package hierarchy decide the program's structure
**The Dictionary and CDS model the data**: A business entity is defined once and used by reports, services, and the UI

learning.text: **The language and the platform are learned together**: A newcomer learns the syntax, the Dictionary, the transport system, and the business model at once
**The surface is large**: Classic procedural syntax, ABAP Objects, CDS, and the RAP framework are four vocabularies
**The documentation is exhaustive**: SAP's keyword documentation covers the language in detail

syntax.text: **The syntax is sentence-like and verbose**: `DATA`, `TYPE`, and `WRITE` spell out what a C-family language infers from punctuation
**Two generations share one grammar**: Procedural statements and class-based expressions coexist, and either style can appear in one program
**Constructor expressions are modern**: `NEW`, `VALUE`, `COND`, and `SWITCH` express a value where older code assigned it

testing.text: **ABAP Unit runs inside the system**: A test class is a repository object, and the runner reports in the same session
**The debugger is strong**: A program is stepped, a variable is watched, and a run-time error is analysed in the same session
**ATC checks against a rule set**: The ABAP Test Cockpit applies the rules at transport time
**A test needs a system**: There is no local build and test loop; the test runs in a system with its data

security.text: **Memory is managed**: A program cannot read or write outside its data, and a table read is bounds-checked
**The authorization concept is part of the platform**: An authority check names the object and the field, and the runtime enforces it
**Dynamic SQL and dynamic calls are ordinary statements**: A `WHERE` clause or a method name can be built from a string, so concatenated input is an injection path
**A modification is the risk surface**: A change to a standard object must be re-applied at every upgrade

reproducibility.text: **The artifact is transported, not built**: A program is activated in a system, so the deployed object depends on that system's state and cannot be rebuilt from source alone
**Dependencies are a system level, not a manifest**: A program relies on the `SAP_BASIS` release and on repository objects, and nothing in the source pins them

supplychain.text: **A transport carries no signature**: The import queue moves objects between systems on trust, and a receiver cannot verify who produced them

observability.text: **Trace and statistics are vendor tools**: ST05, SAT, and the ABAP trace are the analysis path, and no open tracing standard is built in
**Logging is a framework API**: The application log is a class library, not a language facility, and a program can write nothing at all

feedback.text: **The syntax check is immediate**: ADT checks a class or a program in the system, so an error is reported without a build

interop.text: **There is no portable target**: The generated code runs only in the ABAP runtime, and a program cannot be shipped to another platform

governance.text: **One vendor governs the language**: SAP defines the syntax, the runtime, and the release schedule, and no independent body ratifies a change
**The specification is a vendor document**: The keyword documentation is authoritative and proprietary, and no public standard defines ABAP

tradeoffs: **Vendor lock-in is the price of the platform**: The Dictionary, the transport system, and the runtime are one product
**Compatibility is kept at the cost of consistency**: Every generation of syntax remains valid, so two idioms coexist indefinitely
**The deployment unit is a transport, not a build**: A program is activated in a system, so the artifact cannot be rebuilt from source alone
**The business model is the language's domain**: A data model is expressed in the Dictionary, and a task outside it needs the runtime's interfaces
**The tooling is integrated and closed**: ADT and the transport system are strong inside SAP and unavailable outside it
verdict: ABAP's design yields high language-imposed coupling. The runtime, the Dictionary, and the vendor own the platform, so the deployment unit is one product. Static typing, ABAP Objects, and managed memory remove several language mechanisms, but the classic return code, the untyped dynamic SQL, the mutable-by-default data, and the absence of a result type keep the error and construction paths open. Main strength: a mature, strongly typed business language with a managed runtime and a strong compatibility promise. Main weakness: a program runs only inside an SAP system, the framework decides the architecture, and the repository carries every generation of the language at once.

energy.text: Runs on the SAP application server; no independent energy or time benchmark for the language is recorded.

ai-readiness.text: Sparse public training data: models write it less reliably than a mainstream language [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.
